title: First-factor localization of derived cohomology over the tensor coefficient ring
statement: Let R,A,Aq,B,D be commutative rings, with R-algebra structures on A,Aq,B, an A-algebra structure on Aq compatible with R, and algebra structures from E=A tensor_R B and E_q=Aq tensor_R B to D. Let Q be a cochain complex of A-modules. Let L and K be base-derived tensor cohomology models [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model] for Q and Aq tensor_A Q respectively, with coefficient B and model parameter D. Let S be a submonoid of A such that Aq is the localization of A at S, and let i be an integer. Let u be a morphism from the underlying R-complex of Q to the underlying R-complex of Aq tensor_A Q whose component sends x to 1 tensor x in every degree [def-pc-ring-tensor-cohomology]. Let phi:E -> E_q be the ring map specified by phi(a tensor b)=algebraMap(A,Aq)(a) tensor b for every a in A and b in B. Let zeta be the unique counit-compatible isomorphism from L.derived to K.derived. Define c:L.cohomology(i) -> K.cohomology(i) as L.cohomologyIso(i).hom, then degree-i cohomology of L.derived(u) followed by zeta at Aq tensor_A Q, then K.cohomologyIso(i).inv. There exists an E_q-linear isomorphism e:E_q tensor_E L.cohomology(i) -> K.cohomology(i) satisfying e(1 tensor x)=c(x) for every x. No compatibility of the maps to D is assumed and no extension to D is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0DJ8, affine localization identity in the proof; Tag 06Y6, derived change of rings

proof.text: Define c by the displayed universal-counit comparison and use the scalar-compatibility theorem to bundle it as an A tensor_R B-linear map to the restriction of K.cohomology(i) along phi.

Mathlib IsLocalization.tensorProduct_tensorProduct identifies Aq tensor_R B as the localization of A tensor_R B at the image T of S. IsLocalization.map_units gives the invertible denominator action. The denominator theorem proves the surj field of IsLocalizedModule T c; apply the kernel theorem to x-y to prove its exists_of_eq field.

Apply IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange and IsBaseChange.equiv to get the Aq tensor_R B-linear equivalence, then toModuleIso. IsBaseChange.equiv_tmul at coefficient one gives exactly the displayed generator formula, by unfolding c.

theorem exists_firstLocalization_cohomology_baseChange
    (S : Submonoid A) [IsLocalization S Aq] (i : ℤ)
    (Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (L : ModuleCat.BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel R A B Q D)
    (K : ModuleCat.BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel R Aq B ((extend A Aq).obj Q) D)
    (uQ : (restrict R A).obj Q ⟶ (restrict R Aq).obj ((extend A Aq).obj Q))
    (huQ : ∀ (j : ℤ) (x : Q.X j), uQ.f j x = (1 : Aq) ⊗ₜ[A,algebraMap A Aq] x) :
    letI := L.universal
    letI := K.universal
    let ζ := Functor.leftDerivedNatIso L.derived K.derived L.counit K.counit
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} R) (.up ℤ)) (Iso.refl _)
    ∃ e : (ModuleCat.extendScalars
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aq)
          (AlgHom.id R B)).toRingHom).obj (L.cohomology i) ≅ K.cohomology i,
      ∀ x : L.cohomology i,
        e.hom ((1 : Aq ⊗[R] B) ⊗ₜ[A ⊗[R] B,
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A Aq)
            (AlgHom.id R B)).toRingHom] x) =
        ((L.cohomologyIso i).hom ≫
          (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} B) i).map
            (L.derived.map (DerivedCategory.Qh.map
              ((HomotopyCategory.quotient (ModuleCat.{u} R) (.up ℤ)).map uQ)) ≫
              ζ.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj
                ((HomotopyCategory.quotient (ModuleCat.{u} R) (.up ℤ)).obj
                  ((restrict R Aq).obj ((extend A Aq).obj Q))))) ≫
          (K.cohomologyIso i).inv) x
